newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips, with PC manufacturers giving ground.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips, with PC manufacturers giving ground.

text.p: Nasdaq shares slipped on Monday in light trading, with a continuation of Friday's selloff in some personal computer manufacturers amid concerns over profit margins and price pressures, traders said.
The Nasdaq composite index fell 6.05 points, or 0.39 percent, to close unofficially at 1563.53. Advancing issues narrowly beat decliners on total volume of 596 million shares.

Dell Computer Corp, the most active Nasdaq issue, fell 2-5/8 to 78-7/8 on the stock's first post-split session. It had closed at 163 Friday after dropping seven points. Gateway 2000 Inc fell 11/16 to 39-11/16.

"Today was a continuation of Friday when PC manufacturers showed weakness," one trader said, adding concerns over margins and price-cutting lingered from Gateway's release of second quarter earnings on Friday.
"Volume was lighter than usual. The market basically took a rest today, but sold off later in the day when the Big Board started to come off, another trader said."
Chips and Technologies Inc jumped 3-1/16 to 17-1/16 after Intel said it agreed to acquire the company in a cash tender of $17.50 per share, $3.50 above Friday's Nasdaq closing price.

Cisco Systems Inc fell 2-5/16 to 77-3/8 after the company said its near-term earnings would be dampened by the $125 million acquisition of the high-speed networking business of Integrated Network Corp.
